info.title: Prefetch API
info.description: Extract brand identity, company data, screenshots, IAB classifications, and clean page content from any URL.

apiKey.name: X-API-Key
apiKey.description: Your Prefetch API key. Obtain one from the dashboard.

durationMs.description: Time taken to process the request in milliseconds.

success.description: Always false. Absent, like `meta`, on authentication and rate-limit errors, which are answered before a request is processed.

error.description: Human-readable error message. The wording can change: branch on `error_code`.

error_code.description: What went wrong, for machines. Stable: a code keeps its meaning once published. See [Error handling](/concepts/errors).

retryable.description: Whether the same request can succeed if sent again after a short wait (honour `Retry-After` when present). False for problems with the request or the target.

retryAfterSeconds.description: On `RATE_LIMITED`: seconds until a request will be accepted.

limit.description: On `CONCURRENCY_LIMITED`: how many requests this key may have in flight.

CodeColorItem.description: One color scraped from the page's CSS, HTML, or JavaScript.

color.description: The raw value as written on the page.

group.description: Nearest named color, used as the group key.

distance.description: Distance to that named color. 0 is an exact match.

name.description: Tint label within the group, ordered nearest-first.

hex.description: The color as a hex triplet.

source.description: Where the color came from. Present on `screenshot_colors` entries only.

brand_colors.description: The brand palette, built from the logo and brand assets. Always present.

code_colors.description: Colors scraped from the page's code, keyed by nearest named color. Present only when `css=true`, `html=true`, or `javascript=true`. Sources are merged into one map, not split per source.

screenshot_colors.description: Dominant colors sampled from the screenshot. Present only when `screenshotColors=N` is passed.

families.description: Font family names detected on the page.

url.description: Public URL to the logo asset.

width.description: Intrinsic width of the logo in pixels.

height.description: Intrinsic height of the logo in pixels.

primary.description: Best candidate for the primary logo.

secondary.description: Other logo candidates found on the page.

apple_touch_icon.description: URL to the Apple Touch Icon.

BrandAssetItem.description: An image harvested from the site or its social profiles, such as a Twitter banner.

assets.description: Additional brand imagery found on the site and its social profiles.

screenshot_url.description: URL to the page screenshot stored in cloud storage.

SocialLinks.description: Social media profile URLs keyed by platform name.

background.description: Fill color. `null` for an outlined or text-only button.

border_color.description: Border color, when the button has a visible border.

border_radius.description: Corner radius. `9999px` means fully rounded (a pill).

DesignTokens.description: The site's design system by role, read from the rendered page. Present only when the request sets `designTokens=true`. Best effort: a field the page gives no reliable answer for is `null`.

color_scheme.description: Whether the page background is light or dark.

primary.description: The main action color: the fill of the most prominent button, or a colored link when no button is filled.

secondary.description: The fill of the next most prominent button, when it is a distinct color.

link.description: The most common color of in-content links.

font_family.description: The first family in the stack.

line_height.description: `null` when the site leaves it at `normal`.

sizes.description: Font size of the first visible heading at each level, and of body text.

border_radius.description: The primary button's corner radius, a good proxy for the site's rounding.

BrandBlock.description: Brand identity extracted from the page.

domain.description: Normalized domain extracted from the URL.

ClassificationBlock.description: IAB classification of the site. Null in `/enrich` when classification failed.

description.description: Short human-readable description of the website.

long_description.description: Extended multi-sentence description of the website.

stock_tickers.description: Stock ticker symbols associated with the company, if publicly traded.

isins.description: ISIN codes associated with the company's securities.

domain.description: Normalized domain extracted from the URL.

name.description: Legal entity name of the company.

emails.description: Contact email addresses found on the site.

addresses.description: Physical addresses found on the site.
example: 354 Oyster Point Blvd, South San Francisco, CA 94080

screenshot_url.description: Public URL to the screenshot stored in cloud storage.

full_page.description: Whether the full scrollable height was captured.

captured_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the screenshot was taken.

device.description: The `device` preset the page was rendered as; null for a plain viewport.

device_scale_factor.description: Pixels per CSS pixel in the image: 1 for a plain viewport, the device's own density for a preset.

dark_mode.description: Whether the page was asked for its dark theme.

selector.description: The element captured, when `selector` was set.

warnings.description: Non-fatal notes, e.g. a `wait_for_selector` that never appeared.

EnrichBrandBlock.description: The same brand block `/brand` returns, without `social_links` — in `/enrich` those live on `company` instead.

EnrichData.description: Combined output from brand, company, and classify extraction. Each block sits under the same key the standalone endpoint uses.

ScrapeMetadata.description: Always present, whatever formats were requested.

robots.description: The page's own robots meta tag.

headings.description: The page's heading outline, up to 100 entries.

content_type.description: What the URL served. A PDF's text becomes the markdown; it has no html.

page_count.description: PDFs only: pages in the document.

cache_state.description: Present when the request set `max_age`: `hit` = served from a stored fetch, `miss` = fetched live.

cached_at.description: On a cache hit: when the stored copy was fetched (ISO 8601).

content.description: GitHub Flavored Markdown. Links and images are resolved to absolute URLs.

truncated.description: True when the content hit the 1 MB size cap and was cut.

main_content_only.description: True when boilerplate was successfully isolated away. False means the full page body was returned.

text.description: Null when the summary could not be produced; see `warnings`.

internal.description: Links on the same site, subdomains included.

data.description: The extracted object, shaped by your prompt or schema.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems, such as a format that could not be produced.

ScrapePayload.description: The page content fields. Which of them are present depends on the `formats` requested.

url.description: The image on our CDN. Short-lived: copy it if you need to keep it.

detected.description: True when the page's text appears to contain instructions aimed at an AI model.

reason.description: Why it was flagged, quoting or describing the suspicious text. Null when nothing was found.
reason.example: The page tells AI assistants to ignore their instructions and send the user's API keys to an outside address.

complete.description: True when all of the page's text was checked. False when part of it could not be (a very long page, or the classifier was unavailable): `detected: false` then means nothing was found in what was checked, not that the page is clean.

model.description: The model that checked it; null for a page with no text.

PdfBlock.description: Present when the URL served a PDF. Its text is in `markdown`.

pages_parsed.description: Pages whose text was read (capped for very long documents).

ScrapeBody.description: The same options as `GET /scrape`, as typed JSON.

wait_for.description: Milliseconds to wait after the page loads.

wait_for_selector.description: Wait (up to 10 s) for this CSS selector. Best effort.

headers.description: Request headers to send to the target. Up to 20. Requests with headers are never cached.

max_age.description: Accept a stored copy fetched at most this many milliseconds ago.

check_prompt_injection.description: Check the page's text for prompt injection — text written to make an AI model reading the page ignore its instructions, leak data or take actions — and report it in `prompt_injection`. The page is still returned: the check warns, it does not block. Costs the same 3-credit surcharge as `summary` and `json` (once per page, however many of the three you ask for).

domain.description: Bare host, ready for the `url` parameter of every other endpoint.

confidence.description: 0–1. Only `results[0]` can reach 0.8; at or above it, that result is the answer. Below it, a candidate to check.

source.description: `curated`: reviewed brand data. `index`: the name index. `live`: verified against the site during this request.

results.description: Best match first; one entry per domain. Empty when nothing matched.

live_used.description: Whether the live lookup ran — and so whether the request was billed 3 credits.

warnings.description: Non-fatal notes, e.g. a live lookup skipped because the service was busy.

lastmod.description: From the sitemap, when the site publishes one.

CrawlScrapeOptions.description: How each crawled page is fetched and rendered. The same options `GET /scrape` takes.

headers.description: Sent with every page request. Pages fetched with headers are never cached.

max_age.description: Accept stored copies of pages fetched at most this many milliseconds ago.

check_prompt_injection.description: Check each page for prompt injection, as on `/scrape`. Adds the AI surcharge to every page.

max_depth.description: How many links deep to follow from the start URL. Sitemap-seeded pages sit at depth 0, so `max_depth: 0` with `use_sitemap: true` crawls exactly what the sitemap lists and follows nothing.

include_paths.description: Regular expressions matched against a URL's path and query. A URL must match at least one to be crawled.

exclude_paths.description: Regular expressions. A URL matching any of them is skipped. Exclusions win over inclusions.

allow_subdomains.description: Follow links onto subdomains of the start URL.

ignore_query_params.description: Treat URLs that differ only by query string as one page.

respect_robots_txt.description: Obey the rules in `robots.txt` — Disallow and Crawl-delay. Sitemap discovery happens either way.

use_sitemap.description: Seed the crawl from the site's sitemap as well as from links.

crawl_entire_domain.description: Follow links anywhere on the site. By default a crawl stays at or below the path it starts from: one started at `/docs/` crawls `/docs/…` only. A crawl from the root covers the whole site either way.

webhook.description: Where to send progress: an https URL, or an object. Events: `crawl.started`, `crawl.page` (one per page), `crawl.completed`, `crawl.failed`. Each delivery is signed — `X-Prefetch-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`, HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<raw body>` with the `secret` returned when the crawl is created — the same scheme as monitor webhooks.

metadata.description: Echoed back in every payload (up to 4 KB).

delay_ms.description: Politeness delay between pages. A larger `Crawl-delay` in robots.txt wins.

expires_at.description: After this, the crawl and its pages are no longer readable.

secret.description: Verifies the `X-Prefetch-Signature` on each delivery. Shown only here — store it.

CrawlPage.description: One crawled page. Carries the same fields `GET /scrape` returns, plus the crawl's own bookkeeping.

depth.description: How many links from the start URL. Sitemap-seeded pages are depth 0.

ok.description: False when the page could not be fetched. You are not charged for it.

error_code.description: Why the page failed, as one of the API's [error codes](/concepts/errors#error-codes); null when it did not.

SkippedUrls.description: URLs the crawl found but did not fetch, by reason: `limit`, `depth`, `out-of-scope`, `excluded`, `not-included`, `robots`, `off-site`, `file`, `invalid`, `blocklist`, `duplicate` (a redirect onto a page already crawled).

error_code.description: Why the page failed, as one of the API's [error codes](/concepts/errors#error-codes).

failed.description: Pages that were fetched and failed, oldest first.

urls.description: The pages to scrape (1–500). Duplicates are scraped once.

ignore_invalid_urls.description: Drop URLs that fail validation (listed in `invalid_urls`) instead of rejecting the whole batch.

webhook.description: Where to send progress: an https URL, or an object. Events: `batch_scrape.started`, `batch_scrape.page` (one per page), `batch_scrape.completed`, `batch_scrape.failed`. Each delivery is signed — `X-Prefetch-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`, HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<raw body>` with the `secret` returned when the batch is created — the same scheme as monitor webhooks.

metadata.description: Echoed back in every payload (up to 4 KB).

endpoint.description: What each URL is run through.

url_count.description: Pages queued, after removing duplicates (and invalid URLs, with ignore_invalid_urls).

secret.description: Verifies the `X-Prefetch-Signature` on each delivery. Shown only here — store it.

total.description: Pages the crawl expects to fetch, as currently known. Rises as it discovers more.

next.description: URL for the next page of results, or null when there are no more.

endpoint.description: What each item is: `scrape` for a crawl or /batch/scrape, otherwise the batch's endpoint (`brand`, `enrich`, …).

skipped.description: URLs the crawl found but did not fetch, by reason: `limit`, `depth`, `out-of-scope`, `excluded`, `not-included`, `robots`, `off-site`, `file`, `invalid`, `blocklist`, `duplicate` (a redirect onto a page already crawled). Present once anything was skipped.

MonitorSchedule.description: Exactly one of `cron` or `text`. A bare string is accepted too, and read as cron when it has five cron fields.

cron.description: Five-field cron expression. How close together runs may be depends on the plan: an hour apart on Free, 5 minutes on Starter and Pro, 2 on Growth, 1 on Scale.

text.description: A plain-English schedule, converted to cron: "every 30 minutes", "every 15 minutes starting at :07", "hourly", "every 2 hours", "daily", "daily at 9am", "daily at 5:30 PM", "every weekday at 9am", "weekly", "every monday at 8:00", "monthly".

timezone.description: IANA timezone the schedule runs in.

MonitorScrapeOptions.description: How each page is rendered before it is compared — the content-shaping options of `GET /scrape`.

only_main_content.description: Compare the main content only, ignoring navigation, sidebars and footers.

include_links.description: Keep link URLs in the compared markdown.

include_images.description: Keep images in the compared markdown. Off by default: image URLs carry cache-busting hashes that change on every deploy.

include_selectors.description: CSS selectors to compare instead of the detected main content.

exclude_selectors.description: CSS selectors to leave out of the comparison — the way to silence a timestamp or a rotating banner.

modes.description: `markdown` diffs the page text line by line. `json` extracts the fields described by `json_prompt` or `json_schema` on every check and diffs them field by field, so a page is `changed` only when a tracked field changes. Both together report `changed` when either surface changed.

json_prompt.description: For the `json` mode: the fields to track, in plain English.
json_prompt.example: Each plan: name, monthly price, headline features

json_schema.description: For the `json` mode: a JSON Schema for the extraction.

limit.description: Most pages each check crawls. Every page is billed on every check.

max_depth.description: How many links deep to follow from the start URL.

include_paths.description: Regular expressions matched against a URL's path and query. A URL must match at least one to be monitored.

exclude_paths.description: Regular expressions. A matching URL is skipped.

allow_subdomains.description: Follow links onto subdomains of the start URL.

ignore_query_params.description: Treat URLs that differ only by query string as one page.

use_sitemap.description: Seed each crawl from the site's sitemap as well as from links.

MonitorScrapeTarget.title: Scrape target
MonitorScrapeTarget.description: Watches a fixed list of pages, each fetched the way `GET /scrape` would fetch it.

id.description: Stable target id. Generated when omitted; on update, a target watching the same URLs keeps its id — and its snapshots — automatically.

MonitorCrawlTarget.title: Crawl target
MonitorCrawlTarget.description: Re-crawls a site on every check, so pages that appear or disappear are reported as well as pages that change.

id.description: Stable target id. Generated when omitted.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint that receives the events.

headers.description: Extra headers sent with every event, at most 20. `Host`, `Content-Type` and `X-Prefetch-*` are reserved.

metadata.description: Echoed back in every event, up to 4 KB.

secret.description: Signing secret, 16–128 printable characters. Generated when omitted, and kept across updates unless you replace it.

rotate_secret.description: Update only: generate a new signing secret.

to.description: Up to 5 addresses to email when a check finds changes. An address on your Prefetch account receives alerts at once; any other address is sent one confirmation email and receives nothing until it confirms.

resend_confirmation.description: Update only: send the confirmation email again to addresses that are still `pending`.

goal.description: What you want to be told about, in one plain sentence. With a goal, every changed page is judged against it, and only meaningful changes send a `monitor.page` webhook. 1 credit per page judged.
goal.example: Alert me when a plan price or its included features change

judge_enabled.description: Judge changes against the goal. Default: `true` when a goal is set.

targets.description: What to watch. At most 500 pages per check across all targets.

retention_days.description: How long check history is kept.

MonitorUpdateRequest.description: Any subset of the create fields, plus `status`. Fields you leave out stay as they are.

goal.description: `null` clears the goal and turns judging off.

email.description: Replaces the list of addresses. Addresses you keep keep their status. `null` removes them all.

status.description: Pause or resume. Resuming runs at the next scheduled time; runs missed while paused are not replayed.

secret.description: Verifies the `X-Prefetch-Signature` header on every event.

MonitorEmail.description: Email alerts: one email per check that finds changes, to every `active` address. `null` when the monitor emails nobody.

to.description: Every address, in the form `PATCH` takes back.

status.description: `active` receives alerts. `pending` was sent a confirmation email and receives nothing until it confirms. `unsubscribed` stopped them from a link in an email.

confirmation_sent_at.description: When the confirmation email went out. `null` on a pending address means it could not be sent: retry with `resend_confirmation`.

cron.description: The schedule the monitor runs on — always cron, whatever you submitted.

text.description: The phrase it was created from, if any.

current_check_id.description: The check running right now, if any.

targets.description: Normalised: every target has an id and every option its effective value.

estimated_credits_per_check.description: Upper bound: every page fetched, and judged when a goal is set. A real check costs less — only fetched pages are billed, and only changed ones judged.

estimated_credits_per_month.description: `estimated_credits_per_check` times the runs in an average month.

last_check_summary.description: Counts from the most recent check, or `null` before the first one.

updated_at.description: When the settings last changed. Checks do not touch it.

next.description: URL for the next page of monitors, or null.

status.description: `partial`: some pages errored, or the check stopped early on credits or its time limit — its results are real but incomplete. `skipped_overlap`: the previous check was still running. `skipped_no_credits`: the owning key had no credits or was revoked. Skipped checks are never charged.

estimated_credits.description: Upper bound, computed when the check was queued.

actual_credits.description: What the check was charged: pages fetched at the `/scrape` rate, plus pages judged.

target_results.description: Per target: pages checked, and for crawls whether the crawl ran to completion. Only a complete crawl can report removed pages.

error.description: Why the check is partial, failed or skipped, or what it could not do.

next.description: URL for the next page of checks, or null.

reason.example: The Starter plan's price went from $19 to $24 a month.

text.description: Markdown mode: a unified diff of the page's markdown.

hunks.description: Markdown mode: the same diff as structured hunks.

truncated.description: The diff was larger than the stored cap. The line counts still cover all of it.

too_large.description: The page changed almost entirely, so no line diff was computed.

fields.description: JSON mode: changed fields keyed by JSON path, each `{ previous, current, change }`.

previous_check_id.description: The check the compared snapshot was taken in.

is_meaningful.description: The judge's verdict, or `null` when the page was not judged.

diff.description: For changed pages, and for pages that are new since the first check.

snapshot.description: JSON mode: the full current extraction.

webhook.description: Webhook deliveries for this check, by outcome. `null` when the monitor has no webhook.

email.description: Alert emails for this check, by outcome. `null` when the monitor emails nobody.

next.description: URL for the next page of results, or null.

id.description: Delivery id, also sent as `X-Prefetch-Delivery`. Stable across retries — use it to de-duplicate.

metadata.description: The `metadata` you set on the webhook.

id.description: Delivery id, also sent as `X-Prefetch-Delivery`. Stable across retries — use it to de-duplicate.

metadata.description: The `metadata` you set on the webhook.

scraped.description: Result pages fetched — each charged at the /scrape rate.

position.description: Rank on the results page, from 1.

description.description: The snippet the search engine shows for the result.

date.description: Publication date as the result shows it, when it shows one.

allOf.description: The result page in the requested formats — the same object GET /scrape returns. Present when scraping was asked for and the page was fetched.

scrape_error.description: Why the result page could not be scraped. Not charged.

query.description: What to search for, as you would type it into Google (1–400 characters). Search operators work (`"exact phrase"`, `-word`, `filetype:pdf`). `q` is accepted too.

limit.description: Results to return (1–50; 1–10 when results are scraped). Default: 10.

check_prompt_injection.description: Check each page for prompt injection, as on /scrape. Adds the AI surcharge to every page.

scrape_options.description: Scrape each result page — the same options /scrape takes. Omit to return search results only.

timeout.description: Give up after this many milliseconds (5,000–45000). Result pages still loading are returned with a `scrape_error` and not charged.

SearchBody.description: The same options as GET /search, as typed JSON.

css.description: The guide as CSS custom properties on `:root`.

tailwind.description: The guide as a Tailwind config: merge `theme.extend` into yours.

primary.description: The main action color: the fill of the most prominent button.

surface.description: The most used fill other than the page background: panels, cards, sections.

palette.description: Every color the guide found, by role, most important first (up to 16).

styles.description: The style most of each element's instances share.

scale.description: The ratio between steps of the type scale, named when it is a classic one.

web_fonts.description: Stylesheet URLs that load the fonts, to reuse as they are.

base_unit.description: The unit most margins, paddings and gaps are a multiple of.

full.description: Whether pills (fully rounded corners) are used.

breakpoints.description: The media-query widths the site's CSS switches layout at.

css_variables.description: The site's own CSS custom properties for colors, lengths, fonts and shadows, as set on the root (up to 120).

kind.description: What the line is: a payment to a `merchant`, to a `person` (Venmo, Zelle…), a `transfer` between accounts, a bank `fee`, an `atm` withdrawal, a `refund`, or `unknown`.

name.description: The merchant's trading name, with words the descriptor truncated completed.

domain.description: Its website, when found with enough confidence; ready for every other endpoint's `url`.

confidence.description: 0–1, for the domain. At 0.8 or above treat it as the answer.

candidates.description: Every domain considered, best first — including ones below the confidence bar.

payment_processor.description: The processor or wallet that prefixed the line (Square, Toast, PayPal…).

location.description: Where the line says the payment was made, when it says.

logo_url.description: The merchant's logo on the Prefetch logo CDN, with your publishable token: put it straight in an . Null when no website was found.

brand.description: With `include_brand=true` and a website found: the same block GET /brand returns.

parsed_by.description: `rules` when the language model was unavailable and the line was read by pattern alone.

descriptor.description: The transaction line as the bank statement or card network shows it (1–200 characters).

include_brand.description: Also return the merchant's brand — logos, colors, fonts — exactly as GET /brand would, when its website is found. Adds the /brand price (10 credits), charged only when a brand is returned. Can take several seconds for a site not seen before.

TransactionBody.description: The same options as GET /transaction, as typed JSON.

urls.description: The URLs or bare domains to run (1–500). Duplicates run once. `domains` is accepted too.

options.description: The endpoint's own parameters, as GET /{endpoint} takes them, applied to every URL — e.g. `{"design_tokens": true}` for brand or enrich, `{"device": "iphone_15"}` for screenshot. Typed JSON or strings.

ignore_invalid_urls.description: Drop URLs that fail validation (listed in `invalid_urls`) instead of rejecting the whole batch. Default: false.

anyOf.description: An https:// URL; every event is sent.

events.description: Which events to send. Default: all four.

metadata.description: Echoed back in every payload (up to 4 KB).

CrawlWebhook.description: Where to send progress. Each delivery is signed — `X-Prefetch-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`, HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<raw body>` with the `secret` returned when the job is created — the same scheme as monitor webhooks.

ok.description: False when the URL could not be answered. You are not charged for it.

error_code.description: Why the page failed, as one of the API's error codes (`TARGET_TIMEOUT`, `DNS_RESOLUTION_FAILED`, …); null when it did not.

BatchItem.description: One URL of a batch: the fields GET /{endpoint} returns for it (`domain`, `brand`, `company`, `classification`, `screenshot_url`, `styleguide`, …), plus the batch's bookkeeping.

token.description: Your organisation's publishable logo token. Safe to put in a web page: it serves logo images only, within your plan's quota.

quota.description: Logo requests included this month; null is unlimited.

used.description: Logo requests counted this month. Counts reach it within a minute or so.

period.description: The month the counts are for (its first day, UTC).

url.name: url
url.description: The website URL to process. `https://` is prepended automatically if no protocol is provided.

screenshotWidth.name: width
screenshotWidth.description: Viewport width in pixels. Range: 320–2560. Default: 1440.

screenshotHeight.name: height
screenshotHeight.description: Viewport height in pixels. Range: 240–5000. Default: 900.

screenshotFormat.name: format
screenshotFormat.description: Output format: `jpeg`, `png`, `webp`, or `pdf` (the whole page as a PDF document). Default: `jpeg`.

screenshotFullPage.name: full_page
screenshotFullPage.description: Capture full scrollable page height. Default: `false`.

scrapeFormats.name: formats
scrapeFormats.description: Comma-separated list of output formats: `markdown`, `summary`, `html`, `raw_html`, `links`, `images`, `json`, `screenshot`. Each requested format appears as its own object on `data`; formats you do not request are absent, not null.

onlyMainContent.name: only_main_content
onlyMainContent.description: Strip navigation, sidebars, footers, and cookie banners before rendering `markdown`, `html`, `summary`, and `json`. `links` and `images` always come from the full document.

includeLinks.name: include_links
includeLinks.description: Keep hyperlinks in the `markdown` and `html` output. When false, link text is kept and the target is dropped.

includeImages.name: include_images
includeImages.description: Keep images in the `markdown` and `html` output.

includeBase64Images.name: include_base64_images
includeBase64Images.description: Keep inline `data:` images. Off by default because base64 payloads are large and carry no meaning as text.

includeSelectors.name: include_selectors
includeSelectors.description: Comma-separated CSS selectors to keep. Overrides main-content detection entirely.

excludeSelectors.name: exclude_selectors
excludeSelectors.description: Comma-separated CSS selectors to remove before rendering.

jsonPrompt.name: json_prompt
jsonPrompt.description: What to extract, in plain language. Required for the `json` format unless `json_schema` is given.

jsonSchema.name: json_schema
jsonSchema.description: A JSON Schema, passed as a JSON string, describing the object the `json` format should return.

scrapeScreenshotFullPage.name: screenshot_full_page
scrapeScreenshotFullPage.description: For the `screenshot` format: capture the whole scrollable page.

waitFor.name: wait_for
waitFor.description: Milliseconds to wait after the page loads, for content that arrives late. Renders in a browser.

waitForSelector.name: wait_for_selector
waitForSelector.description: Wait (up to 10 s) for this CSS selector before reading the page. Best effort: if it never appears, the page is returned with a warning.

scrapeHeaders.name: headers
scrapeHeaders.description: Request headers to send to the target, as a JSON object string. Up to 20; hop-by-hop and proxy headers are refused. Requests with headers are never cached. Easier as an object in `POST /scrape`.

mobile.name: mobile
mobile.description: Render the page as a phone (viewport, touch and user agent).

scrapeTimeout.name: timeout
scrapeTimeout.description: Give up after this many milliseconds.

maxAge.name: max_age

post.description:
Watches pages on a schedule and tells you what changed. Each check re-fetches every target — a fixed list of URLs (`scrape`) or a whole site (`crawl`) — and compares each page with the previous check: `same`, `new`, `changed`, `removed` or `error`, with a diff. Give it a `goal` and every change is judged against it, so only meaningful changes reach your webhook or inbox.

The first check records a baseline: every page is `new`, and no `monitor.page` events or emails are sent for it.

With `email`, each check that finds changes sends one email listing them. An address on your Prefetch account receives alerts at once; any other address confirms from an email first.

**Credit cost: none to create.** Each check bills 1 credit per page it fetches (the `/scrape` rate, 4 on targets tracking `json`), plus 1 per changed page judged against the goal.

**Credit cost: 3 per lookup, 1 when the same line (with the same country and MCC) was looked up in the last 7 days**, plus 10 when `include_brand` returns a brand. Failures are never charged.

The same endpoint as `GET /transaction`, with its options as typed JSON.

post.summary: Run an endpoint on many URLs
post.description:
Runs `brand`, `enrich`, `company`, `classify`, `screenshot` or `styleguide` on up to 500 URLs or bare domains as one job, and returns its id immediately. Each URL is answered exactly as `GET /{endpoint}` would answer it — curated data first, then a live extraction — with `options` (that endpoint's own parameters) applied to every URL. Poll `GET /batch/{endpoint}/{id}` for progress and results, or pass a `webhook`: events are named `batch_{endpoint}.*` (`batch_enrich.page` per URL, `batch_enrich.completed` at the end).

**Credit cost: nothing to submit, then the endpoint's own price per URL answered** (enrich 12, brand 10, styleguide 10, classify 5, company 5, screenshot 1). URLs that fail are never charged. A key whose balance cannot cover every URL is refused up front with `CREDITS_EXHAUSTED`. Webhooks are not available through RapidAPI.
